differencesToBaseline: Current return pitch was 0, whereas all three retain downward pitch.
Current controller releases all movement during turns. iiNavy demonstrates coordinated lateral/back input.
Current F3 approach infers landing from height and block success from Looking at; telemetry can verify actual onGround and block occupancy.
Reference bridges visibly rise; baseline flat-only test should not be called Speed Telly success.
status: 1.8.3 installed-app visual comparison complete; cardinal functional runs recorded in app-1.8.3-trials.json. No claim of indistinguishability from human input.

ownAppComparison.method: Single-window ScreenCaptureKit capture, no desktop/audio; AVAssetReader actual unique sample timestamps. Inspected 48 frames at 4.0–4.8 s and enlarged 13-frame return/next-turn interval.
findings: The return spans about 33 ms between the observed endpoint frames, with only one intermediate direction. It remains visibly faster than the approximately 67 ms iiNavy reference return interval.
Yaw and pitch change together, without random jitter. Forward view remains downward, consistent with all three inspected reference clips.
The overall repeated cycle is about 0.45 s in this interval, comparable in duration to the reference cycles, but equal cycle duration does not establish human-like motion.
Placement tracking includes conspicuous downward corrections near the last block. Further smoothing must be retested against the now working installed-app cardinal runs.
ownAppComparison.acceptance: Functional cardinal validation passed; naturalness not yet accepted.

observations: Three visible intermediate directions now connect the endpoint frames; previous 1.8.1 interval had one.
Horizontal turn and pitch change together; no random jitter was added.
The observed duration is close to the roughly 67 ms iiNavy reference interval, within frame-sampling precision.
Landing and takeoff can occur during the return: y=87.0 at 4.4100 and y=87.42 at 4.4600. The controller does not wait an additional full stationary turn before chaining a jump.
limits: This measures a short representative interval, not every turn.
Returning to the original bridge direction remains deliberate; the update does not aim to make automation undetectable.
Reference videos do not expose exact game telemetry.

comparison20261025.observation: During the same placement window yaw crosses the cardinal reverse direction instead of dwelling exactly at 90. Pitch follows the changing placement face. Subsequent return traverses the opposite side. Integer mouse counts and render sampling can repeat adjacent frames; no claim that every frame differs or resembles any particular player exactly.

installedAppFrames.observations: Confirmed in installed app: placement aim is changing horizontally while its pitch tracks the top/side face, not locked to exact reverse heading. Return approximately 6.075–6.1617 and next outbound approximately 6.1967–6.3167 move in opposite directions. Some adjacent frames repeat; observations are sampled frames, not proof of continuous nonzero velocity at every instant.
